assessment.candidateCrosswalk: BMB 2014/2019 separately list Dagat Dagatan Lake in Tayabas City (24.38 ha) and Lake Pagatan in San Antonio (3.22 ha). The DENR-hosted FASPS plan independently identifies a 2 ha Dagatan Lake in Tayabas, while the official Quezon provincial directory also names a man-made Dagatan Lake in San Antonio. These sources support separate locality-specific Dagatan naming in Tayabas and San Antonio, but do not prove whether the San Antonio Dagatan is the BMB Lake Pagatan.
assessment.stillUnresolved: DENR's 2024 roadmap lists Dagatan Lake and Pagatan Lake separately but gives neither a municipality nor a BMB/site code. Its Dagatan phrase could refer to either the Tayabas or San Antonio locality; the separate Pagatan phrase is not tied to a mapped feature. Do not merge the San Antonio names or assign roadmap phrases without an authoritative crosswalk. The 30 headline versus 31 phrases therefore remains unreconciled.
assessment.tayabasBoundary: Keep the separately inventoried Tayabas City Dagat Dagatan Lake lead distinct; BMB 2014/2019 reports 24.38 ha, while the FASPS plan reports 2 ha. Neither figure is adopted as current geometry.

nextAction: Seek public DENR or Quezon LGU maps, site-code tables, or project records that identify the locality and BMB/site code for each 2024 roadmap phrase, and distinguish San Antonio Dagatan from San Antonio Pagatan. If public records do not resolve this, ask the official Quezon PENRO/CENRO or DENR CALABARZON wetland focal office only after Joseph authorizes an external request; meanwhile keep the full-name Tayabas and San Antonio BMB rows distinct and do not revise the 30-versus-31 denominator.
